gauge.name: Floyd River at Alton

impacts.statement: Hwy 10 is flooded and substantial flooding is ongoing near the river throughout Alton.
Several houses on the north side of Alton flood. Water approaches Hwy 10 on the north side of Alton. The railroad tracks are also flooded.
More substantial street flooding begins in Alton including 3rd Ave south of the bridge. Additional structures are also in danger of flooding.

The lower levees in Alton may begin to be overtopped flooding some nearby industrial businesses. Hwy 60 south of Alton is flooded. Portions of Division St in Alton may also begin to flood and the bridge on 3rd Ave may also be closed.
The entire flood plain is under water and the river is about 1/2 mile wide. The flooding still primarily only affects agricultural land and county roads.
Significant amounts of crop and pasture land are flooded.
410th Street and Larch Avenue is inundated. Also 440th Street and Kingbird Avenue is flooded, and the water reaches the bottom of the bridge at CR L14 and 440th Street.
Flooding begins to affect the lower lying agricultural lands along the river.

value.label: North American Vertical Datum of 1988
value.description: A fixed reference for elevations determined by geodetic leveling. The datum was derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial leveling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 (IGLD 85) local mean sea level height value, at Father Point, Rimouski, Quebec, Canada was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint. NAVD 88 and IGLD 85 are identical. However, NAVD 88 bench mark values are given in Helmert orthometric height units while IGLD 85 values are in dynamic heights. See International Great Lakes Datum of 1985, National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, and geopotential difference. NAVD 88 should not be used as Mean Sea Level.

gauge.forecastReliability: Forecasts are issued as needed during times of high water, but are not routinely available.
